resources.instruction: Update documents only when the change affects visible behaviour, how to install or run, commands, architecture, security posture, the public contract, or a decision a future maintainer needs to know. A purely internal change gets no document or log entry for show. The documents that usually need touching: code conventions, the architecture description, the roadmap, and the changelog if the repository has one. Record an architecture decision as an ADR as flow.sync requires; do not stuff it into a general document.

How to update documents: read the existing documents and the real code before writing, do not describe behaviour you assume. Check that the file names, functions and command-line parameters you mention still exist. Command and code examples must be right: you cannot run commands, so copy from existing tests or scripts instead of inventing them. Delete an outdated section instead of leaving "TODO: update". Compare with related documents so they do not contradict each other. Keep each document file under about 800 lines (a README under 300): beyond that split by topic instead of making it longer. Finally read again what you just wrote: dates, links and every claim must match the real change.
